applicationProfileDefinition.en: Any information that is provided to a procedure for its use.
A workflow,protocol,plan,algorithm,or computational method specifying how to make an Observation.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The procedure explains which steps must be performed to obtain a reproducible result. E.g. the correct placement of an anemometer (at a specific height above the ground surface, e.g. 10m for meteorological observations). The procedures are generally intended to be applied to more than one Observation.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the Input required or used by the procedure.
Reference to the Output that the Procedure generates or generated.
Reference to a document that describes the ObservationProcedure.
Any information that is generated by a procedure.
Device or Agent (including Persons or software) with which Observations are made.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Sensors generate a result based on a stimulus, i.e. a change in the environment, or based on results from other Observations. They are typically hosted by a Platform. Examples are speedometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers mounted on a smart phone. The human eye, for example, can also be regarded as a Sensor.

For example, the coordinates or the address or a reference to a measuring point or other SamplingObject. Several different types of locations can be specified (e.g. address and coordinates). If the Sensor is a measuring installation, possibly the various measuring points that are included or a descriptive polygon. NOTE: The location of the Sensor is not necessarily the position where the Observation takes place, which is primarily given by the location of the SamplingObject or DomainObject. This attribute mainly allows you to describe the positions of sensors, regardless of the measurements that take place.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Determining the value of a certain feature of the traffic at a certain point in time or between two points in time.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Traffic is defined as the movement of objects such as people, freight, data, etc. over modes such as land, water, air, cables. In the context of this application profile, by traffic we mean road traffic. Traffic can refer to objects that move themselves (with or without a means of transport) or objects that are transported, but also to objects over which traffic takes place. The measurement can be the determination of the value of a feature of an individual Vehicle or TrafficParticipant during its movement (e.g. its speed or license plate) or of a feature of the infrastructure such as a RoadSegment or a Lane over which the traffic moves (e.g. the traffic intensity ). TrafficMeasurements are Observations, in other words there is a certain margin of error on the value due to the measuring technique used.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object on which or along which traffic occurs or that is part of traffic.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: ATTENTION: This class is abstract, it must be specialized as a TrafficDomainObject or as a TrafficSamplingObject. As a Traffic DomainObject if the measurement directly relates to the object you want to observe (e.g. a RoadSegment or a Vehicle, etc.) or as a TrafficSamplingObject if the measurement is done indirectly (e.g. via a TrafficMeasuringPoint located along a RoadSegment).

vocabularyDefinition.en: An identifiable instance of a traffic/travel situation comprising one or more traffic/travel circumstances which are linked by one or more causal relationships. Each traffic/travel circumstance is represented by a Situation Record.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: An identifiable instance of a traffic/travel situation comprising one or more traffic/travel circumstances which are linked by one or more causal relationships. Each traffic/travel circumstance is represented by a Situation Record.

vocabularyDefinition.en: More readable representation containing only the basic data of the address,intended for using an address as an attribute of another object.

vocabularyUsageNote.en: Eg as attribute ve person or building. The address representation does not only refer to Belgian addresses, it can be used to represent foreign addresses (where address designations other than house number or bus number may be used or where address components such as address areas occur).

vocabularyDefinition.en: Officially assigned alphanumeric code added to the house number to distinguish multiple building units, pitches, moorings or plots that have the same house number.

vocabularyUsageNote.en: Specialisation of Address Presentation:location indication for Belgian addresses.

vocabularyDefinition.en: Name or description of the geographic object the address locator designates.
Name of a geographic area or place that groups a number of addressable objects to address them without the area or place being an administrative unit.

vocabularyUsageNote.en: For example the name of the hamlet in which the address is located.

vocabularyDefinition.en: Name denoting the geographical area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
The region of address, usually a province or state or similar area that typically includes several places.
Highest Administrative Unit of the address, usually a country.
Country in which the address is located.
Code denoting the geographical area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
The complete address in one string, formatted or not.

vocabularyUsageNote.en: Avoids errors when splitting an address into its components. Displays the prescribed order of the different parts.

vocabularyDefinition.en: PO Box number in a post office.
Alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the address locator within the street, administrative unit, etc.
Alphanumeric code officially assigned to building units, moorings, pitches or plots.

vocabularyUsageNote.en: Specialization of Address representation: location indication for Belgian addresses.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Information used to uniquely identify an object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Idea is that it is a String assigned by an Organisation according to a well-defined identification system.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Link to the agent who assigned the identifier.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: To be used if the agent can be referenced by means of a uri. Use the attribute "assignedBy(String)" otherwise.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Name of the agent who assigned the identifier.
String used to uniquely identify the object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Type of the string refers to the identifier (incl its version), the string itself to the actual identifier.
In essence, a value and the name of the type of the value. E.g.  temperature of 21 degrees Celcius (value = 21 degrees Celcius, name = temperature).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Name of the type of the value.
The quantitative or qualitative value of the NamedValue.
